name: Toilet paper
description: A roll of soft two-ply paper on a card core.
notes: Modelled as a standard 110 mm roll. The model keeps real dimensions, so the box is large against the paper itself.

name: Electric toothbrush
description: A battery toothbrush with a round spinning head.
notes: Battery-powered; its battery and any charge behaviour are left to the electrical items framework. Disassembly could yield a small motor and scrap plastic once those items exist.

name: Toothbrush
description: A plastic toothbrush with soft bristles.
notes: The electric one is electric_toothbrush. cleaning is a new quality name, for brushes, sponges and mops.

name: Hammock
description: A canvas hammock rolled up, with a rope loop at each end for tying between two supports.
notes: Modelled rolled for carrying, the state a player picks up; a hung hammock would be a deployed furniture state with its own model once items can be set up. Sleeping comfort without warmth belongs to that deployed state.

name: Net hammock
description: A cord net hammock gathered into a bundle, with a rope loop at each end.
notes: Bundled netting for carrying, drawn as a cord bundle so it reads apart from the canvas hammock's roll. Same deployed-state note as the hammock.

name: Pewter bowl
description: A footed bowl of dull grey pewter, about a cup deep.
notes: No pewter finish exists; alu-bare stands in for the dull grey metal, with a steel-grey rim. The vessel block omits accepts so any liquid fits.

name: Plastic food tub
description: A frosted plastic food tub with a snap-on watertight lid.
notes: Item id avoids a brand-like name. Many unrelated vessels were once grouped under this one as variants: none of them looks like a lidded plastic tub, and their sizes run from a small bowl to a large pot, so each needs its own model and mass (bowls, jug and tankards share a turned-vessel shape; the hydria, large pot and purifier are large furniture-sized pots). They are listed here so the count stays whole, not because the tub model suits them.

name: Casserole pot
description: A glazed ceramic pot with a domed lid and lug handles, for cooking and serving one-pot meals.
notes: No glaze finish exists; paint-oxblood stands in for the coloured outer glaze and ceramic-white for the rim and knob. Capacity 2.5 L is a judgement from the 200 mm pot.
